fields.originalProduction: Publishing standards Editorial and Puzzle Standards I Love Word Search exists to provide useful free online and printable word search resources. Originality An indexable curated puzzle page should have a distinct purpose, topic-specific word list, stable puzzle definition, unique supporting copy, accurate metadata, and useful related links. Arbitrary user-generated states, search results, and thin variants are not indexed by default. Topic standards Suitable subjects include evergreen general interest, classroom subjects, vocabulary, nature, geography, science, math, language arts, generic holidays, seasons, sports vocabulary, hobbies, food, and animals. Copyrighted characters, celebrity-focused topics, entertainment franchises, and brand-dependent topics require deliberate review. Explicit or hateful content, dangerous instructions, and misleading health claims are not suitable for the general library. Word-list standards Review spelling and topic relevance. Remove duplicates and choose an appropriate difficulty. Check grid fit and audience suitability. Do not add filler terms solely to increase the word count. Description standards Write unique, useful copy rather than lightly spun templates. Avoid keyword stuffing, fake counts, fabricated popularity claims, and unsupported educational or health outcomes. Corrections Visitors can report spelling errors, broken puzzles, print or PDF problems, accessibility issues, unsuitable content, or duplicate pages. Advertising separation If advertising is enabled later, it must remain separate from puzzle controls, never imitate download or navigation buttons, stay out of print and PDF output, avoid obstructing play, and never determine editorial topic selection. The current ad-labelled areas are layout placeholders, not active advertising. Automation and review Software and automation assist with puzzle generation, validation, formatting, and parts of the publishing workflow. Indexable puzzle topics, word lists, and supporting page content are subject to editorial review before they are treated as finished resources.

fields.currentCandidate: FAQ How do I print the puzzle without the surrounding website? Open a puzzle and choose Print this puzzle. Its print view excludes navigation, editing controls and advertisements. Check the preview before printing student copies. How do I keep the answer key off a student copy? In the print or PDF dialog, clear Answer key page for a puzzle-only copy. Keep a separate download with that option selected for checking answers. Which paper setting should I choose? Match US Letter or A4 and the orientation to the paper in your printer. Check the printer preview at actual size; browser or printer scaling can otherwise change the size of the grid and word bank.

fields.currentCandidate: FAQ Why can a large grid still have small letters on paper? A sheet has a fixed printable width. More columns leave less room for each cell, even when a larger display option is selected. Check the downloaded file at actual size and consider a smaller grid with fewer, shorter words. Does choosing larger print move the words? Output sizing alone keeps the current puzzle’s placements. Editing the word list, grid dimensions, seed or directions can create a different puzzle, so keep those settings when you need a matching reprint. What should I check before making several copies? Check both the grid letters and word-bank text, the page margins and the answer page. Make one test copy using the intended paper and printer settings. A large-print label does not guarantee a particular physical text size on every printer.

fields.currentCandidate: FAQ How can I select words with a keyboard? Start a puzzle and focus a grid cell. Arrow keys move between cells. Enter or Space sets the start and submits the end of a straight path; Escape cancels an unfinished selection. Can I tap the first and last letter instead of dragging? Open the solver Settings and choose tap selection. Tap the first cell, then the last cell of a straight word. The word bank marks words that have been found. Can I print the same puzzle after playing online? Yes. Use that puzzle’s print or PDF controls. Its existing seed and configuration determine the grid and answers; switching between play and output does not require generating a different puzzle.

fields.originalProduction: Current site behavior Privacy Policy I Love Word Search does not require an account to create, solve, print, download, or share a puzzle. Browser storage The site uses local browser storage for builder state and puzzle display or output preferences. That information remains in the browser unless you clear it. The current application does not install analytics. Eligible production content pages may load Google AdSense; an explicit emergency setting can disable advertising. Shared puzzle links A share link can encode the puzzle definition needed to reproduce a custom puzzle. It does not include which words a solver has found, reveal progress, or completion progress. Avoid entering private or sensitive information in a word list that you plan to share. PDF and QR behavior PDF files are created by the site’s server endpoint from the submitted puzzle definition. QR images are generated locally in the browser from the share URL; the site does not use an external QR service. Advertising and external links Eligible production content pages load Google AdSense by default, while search, utility, print, PDF, play, answer-key, trust, and legal pages remain ad-free. If advertising is explicitly disabled or Google cannot serve any eligible unit, labelled fallback ad areas may be shown instead. Google may use cookies or similar technologies and process device or interaction data to deliver and measure advertising under Google’s own privacy terms. A Google-certified consent management platform must be configured before personalized ads are enabled where Google requires one. Links to other external sites follow those sites’ own privacy practices. Questions Use the Contact page for a privacy question. The site currently directs contact through the owner’s public portfolio or LinkedIn profile rather than collecting a message through an on-site form.
